  import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
  import getModelAdapter from '@/lib/modelAdapters';
  
  const KNOWN_PROVIDERS = [
    { id: 'claude-cli', label: 'Claude Code CLI' },
    { id: 'ccr', label: 'Claude Code Router (ccr)' },
    { id: 'occ', label: 'Open Claude Code (occ)' },
    { id: 'openclaude', label: 'OpenClaude' },
    { id: 'ollama', label: 'Ollama (local LLM)' },
    { id: 'lm-studio', label: 'LM Studio / OpenAI-compatible' },
    { id: 'openai-http', label: 'OpenAI (HTTP)' },
  ];
  
  export async function GET() {
    try {
      const providers = KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map((p) => {
        const adapter = getModelAdapter(p.id);
        let installedOrConfigured = false;
        let executable = false;
        try {
          installedOrConfigured = !!adapter && adapter.isAvailable();
          executable = !!adapter && (typeof adapter.supportsExecution !==
  'function' || adapter.supportsExecution() !== false);
        } catch {
          installedOrConfigured = false;
          executable = false;
        }
        return {
          id: p.id,
          label: p.label,
          available: installedOrConfigured && executable,
          installedOrConfigured,
          executable,
          note: !executable
            ? 'Provider is discoverable but does not support executable runner
  sessions.'
            : undefined,
        };
      });
  
      return NextResponse.json({ providers });
    } catch (err) {
      return NextResponse.json({ providers: KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map(p => ({ id:
  p.id, label: p.label, available: false, installedOrConfigured: false,
  executable: false })), error: String(err) }, { status: 500 });
    }
  }

  import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
  import getModelAdapter from '@/lib/modelAdapters';
  
  const KNOWN_PROVIDERS = [
    { id: 'claude-cli', label: 'Claude Code CLI' },
    { id: 'ccr', label: 'Claude Code Router (ccr)' },
    { id: 'occ', label: 'Open Claude Code (occ)' },
    { id: 'openclaude', label: 'OpenClaude' },
    { id: 'ollama', label: 'Ollama (local LLM)' },
    { id: 'lm-studio', label: 'LM Studio / OpenAI-compatible' },
    { id: 'openai-http', label: 'OpenAI (HTTP)' },
  ];
  
  export async function GET() {
    try {
      const providers = KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map((p) => {
        const adapter = getModelAdapter(p.id);
        let installedOrConfigured = false;
        let executable = false;
        try {
          installedOrConfigured = !!adapter && adapter.isAvailable();
          executable = !!adapter && (typeof adapter.supportsExecution !==
  'function' || adapter.supportsExecution() !== false);
        } catch {
          installedOrConfigured = false;
          executable = false;
        }
        return {
          id: p.id,
          label: p.label,
          available: installedOrConfigured && executable,
          installedOrConfigured,
          executable,
          note: !executable
            ? 'Provider is discoverable but does not support executable runner
  sessions.'
            : undefined,
        };
      });
  
      return NextResponse.json({ providers });
    } catch (err) {
      return NextResponse.json({ providers: KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map(p => ({ id:
  p.id, label: p.label, available: false, installedOrConfigured: false,
  executable: false })), error: String(err) }, { status: 500 });
    }
  }

  import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
  import getModelAdapter from '@/lib/modelAdapters';
  
  const DEFAULT_MODELS: Record<string, string[]> = {
    'claude-cli': ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5'],
    'ccr': ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5'],
    'occ': ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5'],
    'openclaude': ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5'],
    'openai-http': [process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4o-mini'],
    'lm-studio': [process.env.LM_STUDIO_MODEL || process.env.OPENAI_MODEL ||
  'local-model'],
  };
  
  export async function GET(req: Request) {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url);
      const provider = (url.searchParams.get('provider') ||
  'claude-cli').toLowerCase();
  
      const adapter = getModelAdapter(provider);
      let models: string[] = [];
      let usedDiscovery = false;
      let fallbackUsed = false;
  
      if (adapter && typeof (adapter as any).discoverModels === 'function') {
        try {
          usedDiscovery = true;
          const discovered = await (adapter as any).discoverModels();
          if (Array.isArray(discovered)) models = discovered.filter(Boolean);
        } catch {
          // discovery failed — fall through to fallback
        }
      }
      // If discovery ran and returned an empty list, prefer returning the
      // empty result so the UI can show an explicit 'no models' state. Only
      // fall back to environment/defaults when discovery did not run or
      // failed to produce results.
      if (usedDiscovery && (!models || models.length === 0)) {
        return NextResponse.json({ provider, models: [], modelCount: 0,
  usedDiscovery, fallbackUsed: false });
      }
  
      if ((!models || models.length === 0)) {
        // Discovery was not available or not used — try env-driven defaults
        // and then the built-in DEFAULT_MODELS fallback.
        const envModel = process.env.OPENAI_MODEL;
        const lmStudioModel = process.env.LM_STUDIO_MODEL;
        if (provider === 'openai-http' && envModel) {
          models = [envModel];
        } else if (provider === 'lm-studio' && (lmStudioModel || envModel)) {
          models = [lmStudioModel || envModel || 'local-model'];
        }
        if (!models || models.length === 0) {
          const fallback = DEFAULT_MODELS[provider] ||
  DEFAULT_MODELS['claude-cli'] || [];
          models = fallback.slice();
          fallbackUsed = models.length > 0;
        }
      }
  
      return NextResponse.json({ provider, models, modelCount: models.length,
  usedDiscovery, fallbackUsed });
    } catch (err) {
      return NextResponse.json({ provider: 'unknown', models: [], modelCount: 0,
  error: String(err) }, { status: 500 });
    }

  import {
    AdapterSpawnOptions,
    captureCommandOutput,
    collectConfiguredModelIds,
    commandExists,
    extractLikelyModelIds,
    ModelAdapter,
    spawnLocal,
  } from './ModelAdapter';
  
  /** Adapter for Claude Code Router (`ccr`) wrapper CLI */
  export class ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter implements ModelAdapter {
    private resolveCommand(): string | null {
      if (process.env.CCR_BIN && process.env.CCR_BIN.trim()) {
        return process.env.CCR_BIN.trim();
      }
      if (commandExists('ccr')) return 'ccr';
      return null;
    }
  
    isAvailable(): boolean {
      return Boolean(this.resolveCommand());
    }
  
    supportsExecution(): boolean {
      return true;
    }
  
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions) {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      if (!cmd) {
        throw new Error('`ccr` was not found on PATH. Install/configure Claude
  Code Router first.');
      }
  
      const args = [...(opts.args || [])];
  
      // ccr requires --verbose whenever stream-json is requested.
      const outIdx = args.indexOf('--output-format');
      if (outIdx >= 0 && args[outIdx + 1] === 'stream-json' &&
  !args.includes('--verbose')) {
        args.splice(outIdx, 0, '--verbose');
      }
  
      // In `ccr code --print` mode, passing the prompt via stdin is more
  reliable
      // than positional argv forwarding.
      let promptFromArgs: string | null = null;
      if (args.length > 0) {
        const last = args[args.length - 1];
        if (typeof last === 'string' && !last.startsWith('-')) {
          promptFromArgs = last;
          args.pop();
        }
      }
  
      const child = spawnLocal(cmd, ['code', ...args], opts);
      if (promptFromArgs && child.stdin) {
        child.stdin.write(`${promptFromArgs}\n`);
        child.stdin.end();
      }
      return child;
    }
  
    async discoverModels(): Promise<string[]> {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      const found = new Set<string>(collectConfiguredModelIds());
      if (!cmd) return Array.from(found).sort();
  
      const tries: string[][] = [
        [cmd, 'model', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list'],
        [cmd, 'models', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'models'],
        [cmd, 'list-models'],
        [cmd, '--list-models'],
      ];
  
      for (const t of tries) {
        try {
          const out = await captureCommandOutput(t[0], t.slice(1), { timeoutMs:
  2500 });
          if (!out) continue;
          try {
            const parsed = JSON.parse(out);
            if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
              for (const v of parsed) {
                if (typeof v === 'string') found.add(v);
                if (v && typeof v === 'object' && typeof (v as { id?: unknown
  }).id === 'string') {
                  found.add((v as { id: string }).id);
                }
              }
              continue;
            }
          } catch {
            // non-json output, parse heuristically
          }
  
          for (const token of extractLikelyModelIds(out)) found.add(token);
        } catch {
          // try next command
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    }
  }
  
  export default ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter;

  ---
  
  ## What was happening & what changed
  
  ### Root cause
  The provider/model picker already existed in the codebase and was **already
  fully wired** to the pipeline — when a pipeline starts, the orchestrator reads
  `selectedModel` and `selectedProvider` from the saved state file and assigns
  that model to **all 6 agents** (A, B, C, D, E, S). However, the picker UI was
  wrapped in `{!isPipeline && (...)}` — it was **intentionally hidden** in
  pipeline mode.
  
  ### What was changed
  
  **Both page.tsx and page.tsx:**
  - Removed the `{!isPipeline && (...)}` wrapper that was hiding the picker  
  - Added a **"Provider & Model"** section label (only visible in pipeline mode,
  since manual mode had none)
  - Added `disabled={isPipeline && securityModeLocked}` to all inputs, selects,
  buttons, and checkboxes — they lock automatically once the pipeline starts
  (same as Security Mode and Permission Mode)
  - Added a helper tip in pipeline mode: *"Pipeline agents will all use this
  provider & model. Lock-in once pipeline starts."*
  
  ### How to use it
  1. Switch to **Pipeline** mode
  2. Use the **Provider & Model** section (appears above Security Mode) to pick
  your provider (e.g., LM Studio, Ollama, CCR) and model
  3. Hit **Refresh** to auto-populate models from the selected provider
  4. Start the pipeline — all agents use that model; controls lock until
  pipeline completes/resets

  Completed: *TSC clean check* (6/6)
  
  Everything is in place. Here's a full summary of what was fixed and why:
  
  ---
  
  ## What was fixed
  
  ### 🔴 Bug 1 — Controls permanently greyed out in Pipeline mode
  
  **Root cause**: `securityModeLocked` included `!!state.projectDir`. After any
  completed pipeline run, the state API returns the last project's data
  (including a non-empty `projectDir`) — so on the very next page load,
  `securityModeLocked = true` and every provider/model/security picker becomes
  permanently disabled.
  
  **Fix in both pages**:
  ```typescript
  // Before (buggy — state.projectDir persists forever from completed runs):
  const securityModeLocked = isPipeline && (pipelineStarted || pipelineRunning
  || !!state.projectDir);
  
  // After (correct — only locked while a pipeline is actually in-flight):
  const securityModeLocked = isPipeline && (pipelineStarted || pipelineRunning
  || pipelinePaused);
  ```
  Controls are now freely editable whenever no pipeline is actively running or
  paused.
  
  ---
  
  ### 🔴 Bug 2 — "No staging session" error was silent (console only)
  
  **Root cause**: `handleStartPipeline()` only called `console.error(...)` on
  failure. The user saw nothing in the UI.
  
  **Fix**: Added `pipelineStartError` state to both pages. Errors are now
  displayed inline as a red banner directly above the Start button, with a
  contextual hint for staging/concept errors:
  
  > 💬 **Chat with S first:** describe your project in the Supervisor panel
  below, then click Start.
  
  ---
  
  ### 🟡 UX 3 — No indication that you need to talk to S before starting
  
  **Fix**: Added a guidance note that appears when Pipeline mode is active,
  nothing is running, and no concept has been set yet:
  
  > 💬 **Before starting:** describe your project to **S** (Supervisor) in the
  chat panel below. Once a concept is set, click Start.
  
  This disappears automatically once you've chatted with S and a concept exists
  in the staging state.
  
  ---
  
  **The design intent** is preserved: you must first chat with S (Supervisor) to
  define what you want to build. S writes this to
  `~/Builds/.staging/pipeline-events.json`. Only then does Start Pipeline work.
  The LM Studio models are **not** hardcoded — the app always tries live API
  discovery first, the 23-model list is just the offline fallback.

  import ClaudeCliAdapter from './claudeCliAdapter';
  import OpenAIHttpAdapter from './openaiHttpAdapter';
  import OpenClaudeCodeAdapter from './openClaudeCodeAdapter';
  import OpenClaudeAdapter from './openClaudeAdapter';
  import LMStudioAdapter from './lmStudioAdapter';
  import ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter from './claudeCodeRouterAdapter';
  import OllamaAdapter from './ollamaAdapter';
  import OpenWebUIAdapter from './openWebUIAdapter';
  import OpenAICompatAdapter from './openAICompatAdapter';
  import type { ModelAdapter } from './ModelAdapter';
  
  /**
   * Simple adapter factory for the pipeline runner.
   *
   * Recognizes a small set of well-known provider identifiers and returns a
   * corresponding ModelAdapter instance. Returns null when no matching adapter
   * is known.
   */
  export function getModelAdapter(provider?: string): ModelAdapter | null {
    const p = (provider || 'claude-cli').toLowerCase();
  
    if (p === 'claude-cli' || p === 'claude') {
      return new ClaudeCliAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'occ' || p === 'open-claude-code' || p ===
  '@ruvnet/open-claude-code') {
      return new OpenClaudeCodeAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openclaude' || p === '@gitlawb/openclaude') {
      return new OpenClaudeAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openai-http' || p === 'openai') {
      return new OpenAIHttpAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'lm-studio' || p === 'lmstudio') {
      return new LMStudioAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'ccr' || p === 'claude-code-router') {
      return new ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'ollama') {
      return new OllamaAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openwebui' || p === 'open-webui') {
      return new OpenWebUIAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openai-compat' || p === 'openai-compatible') {
      return new OpenAICompatAdapter();
    }
  
    // Unknown provider
    return null;
  }
  
  export default getModelAdapter;

  /**
   * Read models directly from CCR's config.json — the most reliable source.
   * CCR stores provider configs under ~/.claude-code-router/config.json.
   * Shape: { Providers: [{ name: string, models: string[] }, ...] }
   */
  function readCcrConfigModels(): string[] {
    const configPath = join(homedir(), '.claude-code-router', 'config.json');
    if (!existsSync(configPath)) return [];
    try {
      const raw = readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8');
      const config = JSON.parse(raw) as {
        Providers?: Array<{ name?: string; models?: string[] }>;
        Router?: Record<string, string>;
      };
      const found = new Set<string>();
  
      // Collect all model ids listed under each provider
      if (Array.isArray(config.Providers)) {
        for (const p of config.Providers) {
          if (Array.isArray(p.models)) {
            for (const m of p.models) {
              if (typeof m === 'string' && m.trim()) found.add(m.trim());
            }
          }
        }
      }
  
      // Also extract model names referenced by the Router routes (e.g.
  "lmstudio,model-name")
      if (config.Router && typeof config.Router === 'object') {
        for (const route of Object.values(config.Router)) {
          if (typeof route === 'string') {
            const parts = route.split(',');
            if (parts.length >= 2) {
              const modelPart = parts.slice(1).join(',').trim();
              if (modelPart) found.add(modelPart);
            }
          }
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  }
  
  /** Adapter for Claude Code Router (`ccr`) wrapper CLI */
  export class ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter implements ModelAdapter {
    private resolveCommand(): string | null {
      if (process.env.CCR_BIN && process.env.CCR_BIN.trim()) {
        return process.env.CCR_BIN.trim();
      }
      if (commandExists('ccr')) return 'ccr';
      return null;
    }
  
    isAvailable(): boolean {
      return Boolean(this.resolveCommand());
    }
  
    supportsExecution(): boolean {
      return true;
    }
  
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions) {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      if (!cmd) {
        throw new Error('`ccr` was not found on PATH. Install/configure Claude
  Code Router first.');
      }
  
      const args = [...(opts.args || [])];
  
      // ccr requires --verbose whenever stream-json is requested.
      const outIdx = args.indexOf('--output-format');
      if (outIdx >= 0 && args[outIdx + 1] === 'stream-json' &&
  !args.includes('--verbose')) {
        args.splice(outIdx, 0, '--verbose');
      }
  
      // In `ccr code --print` mode, passing the prompt via stdin is more
  reliable
      // than positional argv forwarding.
      let promptFromArgs: string | null = null;
      if (args.length > 0) {
        const last = args[args.length - 1];
        if (typeof last === 'string' && !last.startsWith('-')) {
          promptFromArgs = last;
          args.pop();
        }
      }
  
      const child = spawnLocal(cmd, ['code', ...args], opts);
      if (promptFromArgs && child.stdin) {
        child.stdin.write(`${promptFromArgs}\n`);
        child.stdin.end();
      }
      return child;
    }
  
    async discoverModels(): Promise<string[]> {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      const found = new Set<string>(collectConfiguredModelIds());
  
      // Primary: read CCR's config.json directly — this is the most reliable
  source
      // because CCR does not expose a machine-readable --list-models CLI flag.
      const configModels = readCcrConfigModels();
      for (const m of configModels) found.add(m);
  
      // If config provided models, return early — no need to call the CLI.
      if (configModels.length > 0) {
        return Array.from(found).sort();
      }
  
      // Fallback: try various CLI flags (these rarely work but worth trying)
      if (!cmd) return Array.from(found).sort();
  
      const tries: string[][] = [
        [cmd, 'model', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list'],
        [cmd, 'models', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'models'],
        [cmd, 'list-models'],
        [cmd, '--list-models'],
      ];
  
      for (const t of tries) {
        try {
          const out = await captureCommandOutput(t[0], t.slice(1), { timeoutMs:
  2500 });
          if (!out) continue;
          try {
            const parsed = JSON.parse(out);
            if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
              for (const v of parsed) {
                if (typeof v === 'string') found.add(v);
                if (v && typeof v === 'object' && typeof (v as { id?: unknown
  }).id === 'string') {
                  found.add((v as { id: string }).id);
                }
              }
              continue;
            }
          } catch {
            // non-json output, parse heuristically
          }
  
          for (const token of extractLikelyModelIds(out)) found.add(token);
        } catch {
          // try next command
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    }
  }
  
  export default ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter;

  export async function GET() {
    try {
      const providers = KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map((p) => {
        const adapter = getModelAdapter(p.id);
        let installedOrConfigured = false;
        let executable = false;

          executable = !!adapter && (typeof adapter.supportsExecution !==
  'function' || adapter.supportsExecution() !== false);
        } catch {
          installedOrConfigured = false;
          executable = false;

          id: p.id,
          label: p.label,
          available: installedOrConfigured && executable,
          installedOrConfigured,
          executable,
          note: !executable
            ? 'Provider is discoverable but does not support executable runner
  sessions.'
            : undefined,
        };
      });
  
      return NextResponse.json({ providers });
    } catch (err) {
      return NextResponse.json({ providers: KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map(p => ({ id:
  p.id, label: p.label, available: false, installedOrConfigured: false,
  executable: false })), error: String(err) }, { status: 500 });
    }
  }

  export function collectConfiguredModelIds(): string[] {
    const found = new Set<string>();
  
    const addValue = (value: unknown) => {
      if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim()) found.add(value.trim());
    };
  
    const addArray = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const item of value) addValue(item);

      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return;

  addValue(key);

  import ClaudeCliAdapter from './claudeCliAdapter';
  import OpenAIHttpAdapter from './openaiHttpAdapter';
  import OpenClaudeCodeAdapter from './openClaudeCodeAdapter';
  import OpenClaudeAdapter from './openClaudeAdapter';
  import LMStudioAdapter from './lmStudioAdapter';
  import ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter from './claudeCodeRouterAdapter';
  import OllamaAdapter from './ollamaAdapter';
  import OpenWebUIAdapter from './openWebUIAdapter';
  import OpenAICompatAdapter from './openAICompatAdapter';
  import type { ModelAdapter } from './ModelAdapter';
  
  /**
   * Simple adapter factory for the pipeline runner.
   *
   * Recognizes a small set of well-known provider identifiers and returns a
   * corresponding ModelAdapter instance. Returns null when no matching adapter
   * is known.
   */
  export function getModelAdapter(provider?: string): ModelAdapter | null {
    const p = (provider || 'claude-cli').toLowerCase();
  
    if (p === 'claude-cli' || p === 'claude') {
      return new ClaudeCliAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'occ' || p === 'open-claude-code' || p ===
  '@ruvnet/open-claude-code') {
      return new OpenClaudeCodeAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openclaude' || p === '@gitlawb/openclaude') {
      return new OpenClaudeAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openai-http' || p === 'openai') {
      return new OpenAIHttpAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'lm-studio' || p === 'lmstudio') {
      return new LMStudioAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'ccr' || p === 'claude-code-router') {
      return new ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'ollama') {
      return new OllamaAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openwebui' || p === 'open-webui') {
      return new OpenWebUIAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openai-compat' || p === 'openai-compatible') {
      return new OpenAICompatAdapter();
    }
  
    // Unknown provider
    return null;
  }
  
  export default getModelAdapter;

  import { ModelAdapter, AdapterSpawnOptions, spawnLocal, captureCommandOutput,
  collectConfiguredModelIds, commandExists, extractLikelyModelIds } from
  './ModelAdapter';
  
  /** Adapter for Gitlawb/openclaude (openclaude) */
  export class OpenClaudeAdapter implements ModelAdapter {
    isAvailable(): boolean {
      return commandExists('openclaude') || commandExists('npx');
    }
  
    supportsExecution(): boolean {
      return true;
    }
  
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions) {
      if (commandExists('openclaude')) {
        return spawnLocal('openclaude', opts.args || [], opts);
      }
      if (commandExists('npx')) {
        return spawnLocal('npx', ['@gitlawb/openclaude', ...(opts.args || [])],
  opts);
      }
      throw new Error('Neither `openclaude` nor `npx` is available.');
    }
  
    async discoverModels(): Promise<string[]> {
      const tries: string[][] = [
        ['openclaude', '--list-models'],
        ['openclaude', 'list-models'],
        ['npx', '@gitlawb/openclaude', '--list-models'],
        ['npx', '@gitlawb/openclaude', 'list-models'],
      ];
  
      const found = new Set<string>(collectConfiguredModelIds());
      for (const t of tries) {
        try {
          const out = await captureCommandOutput(t[0], t.slice(1), { timeoutMs:
  2500 });
          if (!out) continue;
  
          try {
            const parsed = JSON.parse(out);
            if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
              for (const v of parsed) if (typeof v === 'string') found.add(v);
              continue;
            }
          } catch {}
  
          for (const token of extractLikelyModelIds(out)) found.add(token);
        } catch {
          /* ignore */
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    }
  }
  
  export default OpenClaudeAdapter;

  import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
  import { homedir } from 'node:os';
  import { join } from 'node:path';
  import {
    AdapterSpawnOptions,
    captureCommandOutput,
    collectConfiguredModelIds,
    commandExists,
    extractLikelyModelIds,
    ModelAdapter,
    spawnLocal,
  } from './ModelAdapter';
  
  /**
   * Read models directly from CCR's config.json — the most reliable source.
   * CCR stores provider configs under ~/.claude-code-router/config.json.
   * Shape: { Providers: [{ name: string, models: string[] }, ...] }
   */
  function readCcrConfigModels(): string[] {
    const configPath = join(homedir(), '.claude-code-router', 'config.json');
    if (!existsSync(configPath)) return [];
    try {
      const raw = readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8');
      const config = JSON.parse(raw) as {
        Providers?: Array<{ name?: string; models?: string[] }>;
        Router?: Record<string, string>;
      };
      const found = new Set<string>();
  
      // Collect all model ids listed under each provider
      if (Array.isArray(config.Providers)) {
        for (const p of config.Providers) {
          if (Array.isArray(p.models)) {
            for (const m of p.models) {
              if (typeof m === 'string' && m.trim()) found.add(m.trim());
            }
          }
        }
      }
  
      // Also extract model names referenced by the Router routes (e.g.
  "lmstudio,model-name")
      if (config.Router && typeof config.Router === 'object') {
        for (const route of Object.values(config.Router)) {
          if (typeof route === 'string') {
            const parts = route.split(',');
            if (parts.length >= 2) {
              const modelPart = parts.slice(1).join(',').trim();
              if (modelPart) found.add(modelPart);
            }
          }
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  }
  
  /** Adapter for Claude Code Router (`ccr`) wrapper CLI */
  export class ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter implements ModelAdapter {
    private resolveCommand(): string | null {
      if (process.env.CCR_BIN && process.env.CCR_BIN.trim()) {
        return process.env.CCR_BIN.trim();
      }
      if (commandExists('ccr')) return 'ccr';
      return null;
    }
  
    isAvailable(): boolean {
      return Boolean(this.resolveCommand());
    }
  
    supportsExecution(): boolean {
      return true;
    }
  
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions) {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      if (!cmd) {
        throw new Error('`ccr` was not found on PATH. Install/configure Claude
  Code Router first.');
      }
  
      const args = [...(opts.args || [])];
  
      // ccr requires --verbose whenever stream-json is requested.
      const outIdx = args.indexOf('--output-format');
      if (outIdx >= 0 && args[outIdx + 1] === 'stream-json' &&
  !args.includes('--verbose')) {
        args.splice(outIdx, 0, '--verbose');
      }
  
      // In `ccr code --print` mode, passing the prompt via stdin is more
  reliable
      // than positional argv forwarding.
      let promptFromArgs: string | null = null;
      if (args.length > 0) {
        const last = args[args.length - 1];
        if (typeof last === 'string' && !last.startsWith('-')) {
          promptFromArgs = last;
          args.pop();
        }
      }
  
      const child = spawnLocal(cmd, ['code', ...args], opts);
      if (promptFromArgs && child.stdin) {
        child.stdin.write(`${promptFromArgs}\n`);
        child.stdin.end();
      }
      return child;
    }
  
    async discoverModels(): Promise<string[]> {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      const found = new Set<string>(collectConfiguredModelIds());
  
      // Primary: read CCR's config.json directly — this is the most reliable
  source
      // because CCR does not expose a machine-readable --list-models CLI flag.
      const configModels = readCcrConfigModels();
      for (const m of configModels) found.add(m);
  
      // If config provided models, return early — no need to call the CLI.
      if (configModels.length > 0) {
        return Array.from(found).sort();
      }
  
      // Fallback: try various CLI flags (these rarely work but worth trying)
      if (!cmd) return Array.from(found).sort();
  
      const tries: string[][] = [
        [cmd, 'model', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list'],
        [cmd, 'models', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'models'],
        [cmd, 'list-models'],
        [cmd, '--list-models'],
      ];
  
      for (const t of tries) {
        try {
          const out = await captureCommandOutput(t[0], t.slice(1), { timeoutMs:
  2500 });
          if (!out) continue;
          try {
            const parsed = JSON.parse(out);
            if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
              for (const v of parsed) {
                if (typeof v === 'string') found.add(v);
                if (v && typeof v === 'object' && typeof (v as { id?: unknown
  }).id === 'string') {
                  found.add((v as { id: string }).id);
                }
              }
              continue;
            }
          } catch {
            // non-json output, parse heuristically
          }
  
          for (const token of extractLikelyModelIds(out)) found.add(token);
        } catch {
          // try next command
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    }
  }
  
  export default ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter;

  /** Adapter for ruvnet/open-claude-code (occ) */
  export class OpenClaudeCodeAdapter implements ModelAdapter {
    isAvailable(): boolean {
      return commandExists('occ') || commandExists('npx');
    }
  
    supportsExecution(): boolean {
      return true;
    }
  
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions) {
      if (commandExists('occ')) {
        return spawnLocal('occ', opts.args || [], opts);
      }
      if (commandExists('npx')) {
        return spawnLocal('npx', ['@ruvnet/open-claude-code', ...(opts.args ||
  [])], opts);
      }
      throw new Error('Neither `occ` nor `npx` is available for
  open-claude-code.');
    }
  
    async discoverModels(): Promise<string[]> {
      const tries: string[][] = [
        ['occ', '--list-models'],
        ['occ', 'list-models'],
        ['occ', 'models'],
        ['npx', '@ruvnet/open-claude-code', '--list-models'],
        ['npx', '@ruvnet/open-claude-code', 'list-models'],
      ];
      const found = new Set<string>(collectConfiguredModelIds());
      for (const t of tries) {
        try {
          const out = await captureCommandOutput(t[0], t.slice(1), { timeoutMs:
  2500 });
          if (!out) continue;
  
          try {
            const parsed = JSON.parse(out);
            if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
              for (const v of parsed) if (typeof v === 'string') found.add(v);
              continue;
            }
          } catch {}
  
          for (const token of extractLikelyModelIds(out)) found.add(token);
        } catch {
          /* ignore */
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    }
  }
  
  export default OpenClaudeCodeAdapter;

  export async function GET() {
    try {
      const providers = KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map((p) => {
        const adapter = getModelAdapter(p.id);
        let installedOrConfigured = false;
        let executable = false;
        try {
          installedOrConfigured = !!adapter && adapter.isAvailable();
          executable = !!adapter && (typeof adapter.supportsExecution !==
  'function' || adapter.supportsExecution() !== false);
        } catch {
          installedOrConfigured = false;
          executable = false;
        }
        return {
          id: p.id,
          label: p.label,
          available: installedOrConfigured && executable,
          installedOrConfigured,
          executable,
          note: !executable
            ? 'Provider is discoverable but does not support executable runner
  sessions.'
            : undefined,
        };
      });
  
      return NextResponse.json({ providers });
    } catch (err) {
      return NextResponse.json({ providers: KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map(p => ({ id:
  p.id, label: p.label, available: false, installedOrConfigured: false,
  executable: false })), error: String(err) }, { status: 500 });
    }
  }

  export function collectConfiguredModelIds(): string[] {
    const found = new Set<string>();
  
    const addValue = (value: unknown) => {
      if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim()) found.add(value.trim());
    };
  
    const addArray = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const item of value) addValue(item);
    };
  
    const addObjectKeys = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const key of Object.keys(value as Record<string, unknown>))
  addValue(key);
    };
  
    const addObjectValues = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const item of Object.values(value as Record<string, unknown>))
  addValue(item);
    };
  
    for (const filePath of getClaudeSettingsFiles()) {
      const settings = readJsonFile(filePath);
      if (!settings) continue;
      addValue(settings.model);
      addArray(settings.availableModels);
      addObjectKeys(settings.modelOverrides);
      addObjectKeys(settings.agentModels);
      addObjectValues(settings.agentRouting);
  
      const envBlock = settings.env;
      if (envBlock && typeof envBlock === 'object' && !Array.isArray(envBlock))
  {
        const env = envBlock as Record<string, unknown>;
        for (const key of [
          'ANTHROPIC_MODEL',
          'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL',
          'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL',
          'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL',
          'OPENAI_MODEL',
        ]) {
          addValue(env[key]);
        }
      }
    }
  
    for (const key of [
      'ANTHROPIC_MODEL',
      'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL',

    const found = new Set<string>();
    const tokens = text.match(/[A-Za-z0-9:./_\-]{2,}/g) || [];

  import ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter from './claudeCodeRouterAdapter';

  import type { ModelAdapter } from './ModelAdapter';
  
  /**
   * Simple adapter factory for the pipeline runner.
   *
   * Recognizes a small set of well-known provider identifiers and returns a
   * corresponding ModelAdapter instance. Returns null when no matching adapter
   * is known.
   */
  export function getModelAdapter(provider?: string): ModelAdapter | null {
    const p = (provider || 'claude-cli').toLowerCase();
  
    if (p === 'claude-cli' || p === 'claude') {
      return new ClaudeCliAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'occ' || p === 'open-claude-code' || p ===
  '@ruvnet/open-claude-code') {
      return new OpenClaudeCodeAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openclaude' || p === '@gitlawb/openclaude') {
      return new OpenClaudeAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openai-http' || p === 'openai') {
      return new OpenAIHttpAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'lm-studio' || p === 'lmstudio') {
      return new LMStudioAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'ccr' || p === 'claude-code-router') {
      return new ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'ollama') {
      return new OllamaAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openwebui' || p === 'open-webui') {
      return new OpenWebUIAdapter();
    }
  
    if (p === 'openai-compat' || p === 'openai-compatible') {
      return new OpenAICompatAdapter();
    }
  
    // Unknown provider
    return null;
  }
  
  export default getModelAdapter;

  import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

  /**
   * Read models directly from CCR's config.json — the most reliable source.
   * CCR stores provider configs under ~/.claude-code-router/config.json.
   * Shape: { Providers: [{ name: string, models: string[] }, ...] }
   */
  function readCcrConfigModels(): string[] {
    const configPath = join(homedir(), '.claude-code-router', 'config.json');
    if (!existsSync(configPath)) return [];
    try {
      const raw = readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8');
      const config = JSON.parse(raw) as {
        Providers?: Array<{ name?: string; models?: string[] }>;
        Router?: Record<string, string>;
      };
      const found = new Set<string>();
  
      // Collect all model ids listed under each provider
      if (Array.isArray(config.Providers)) {
        for (const p of config.Providers) {
          if (Array.isArray(p.models)) {
            for (const m of p.models) {
              if (typeof m === 'string' && m.trim()) found.add(m.trim());
            }
          }
        }
      }
  
      // Also extract model names referenced by the Router routes (e.g.
  "lmstudio,model-name")
      if (config.Router && typeof config.Router === 'object') {
        for (const route of Object.values(config.Router)) {
          if (typeof route === 'string') {
            const parts = route.split(',');
            if (parts.length >= 2) {
              const modelPart = parts.slice(1).join(',').trim();
              if (modelPart) found.add(modelPart);
            }
          }
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  }
  
  /** Adapter for Claude Code Router (`ccr`) wrapper CLI */
  export class ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter implements ModelAdapter {
    private resolveCommand(): string | null {
      if (process.env.CCR_BIN && process.env.CCR_BIN.trim()) {
        return process.env.CCR_BIN.trim();
      }
      if (commandExists('ccr')) return 'ccr';
      return null;
    }
  
    isAvailable(): boolean {
      return Boolean(this.resolveCommand());
    }
  
    supportsExecution(): boolean {
      return true;
    }
  
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions) {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      if (!cmd) {
        throw new Error('`ccr` was not found on PATH. Install/configure Claude
  Code Router first.');
      }
  
      const args = [...(opts.args || [])];
  
      // ccr requires --verbose whenever stream-json is requested.
      const outIdx = args.indexOf('--output-format');
      if (outIdx >= 0 && args[outIdx + 1] === 'stream-json' &&
  !args.includes('--verbose')) {
        args.splice(outIdx, 0, '--verbose');
      }
  
      // In `ccr code --print` mode, passing the prompt via stdin is more
  reliable
      // than positional argv forwarding.
      let promptFromArgs: string | null = null;
      if (args.length > 0) {
        const last = args[args.length - 1];
        if (typeof last === 'string' && !last.startsWith('-')) {
          promptFromArgs = last;
          args.pop();
        }
      }
  
      const child = spawnLocal(cmd, ['code', ...args], opts);
      if (promptFromArgs && child.stdin) {
        child.stdin.write(`${promptFromArgs}\n`);
        child.stdin.end();
      }
      return child;
    }
  
    async discoverModels(): Promise<string[]> {
      const cmd = this.resolveCommand();
      const found = new Set<string>(collectConfiguredModelIds());
  
      // Primary: read CCR's config.json directly — this is the most reliable
  source
      // because CCR does not expose a machine-readable --list-models CLI flag.
      const configModels = readCcrConfigModels();
      for (const m of configModels) found.add(m);
  
      // If config provided models, return early — no need to call the CLI.
      if (configModels.length > 0) {
        return Array.from(found).sort();
      }
  
      // Fallback: try various CLI flags (these rarely work but worth trying)
      if (!cmd) return Array.from(found).sort();
  
      const tries: string[][] = [
        [cmd, 'model', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'model', 'list'],
        [cmd, 'models', '--json'],
        [cmd, 'models'],
        [cmd, 'list-models'],
        [cmd, '--list-models'],
      ];
  
      for (const t of tries) {
        try {
          const out = await captureCommandOutput(t[0], t.slice(1), { timeoutMs:
  2500 });
          if (!out) continue;
          try {
            const parsed = JSON.parse(out);
            if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
              for (const v of parsed) {
                if (typeof v === 'string') found.add(v);
                if (v && typeof v === 'object' && typeof (v as { id?: unknown
  }).id === 'string') {
                  found.add((v as { id: string }).id);
                }
              }
              continue;
            }
          } catch {
            // non-json output, parse heuristically
          }
  
          for (const token of extractLikelyModelIds(out)) found.add(token);
        } catch {
          // try next command
        }
      }
  
      return Array.from(found).sort();
    }
  }
  
  export default ClaudeCodeRouterAdapter;

  export async function GET() {
    try {
      const providers = KNOWN_PROVIDERS.map((p) => {
        const adapter = getModelAdapter(p.id);
        let installedOrConfigured = false;
        let executable = false;
        try {
          installedOrConfigured = !!adapter && adapter.isAvailable();
          executable = !!adapter && (typeof adapter.supportsExecution !==
  'function' || adapter.supportsExecution() !== false);
        } catch {
          installedOrConfigured = false;
          executable = false;
        }
        return {
          id: p.id,
          label: p.label,
          available: installedOrConfigured && executable,
          installedOrConfigured,
          executable,
          note: !executable
            ? 'Provider is discoverable but does not support executable runner
  sessions.'
            : undefined,
        };
      });
  
      return NextResponse.json({ providers });

  p.id, label: p.label, available: false, installedOrConfigured: false,
  executable: false })), error: String(err) }, { status: 500 });
    }
  }

  export function collectConfiguredModelIds(): string[] {
    const found = new Set<string>();
  
    const addValue = (value: unknown) => {
      if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim()) found.add(value.trim());
    };
  
    const addArray = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const item of value) addValue(item);
    };
  
    const addObjectKeys = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const key of Object.keys(value as Record<string, unknown>))
  addValue(key);
    };
  
    const addObjectValues = (value: unknown) => {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return;
      for (const item of Object.values(value as Record<string, unknown>))
  addValue(item);

      if (!settings) continue;

      addArray(settings.availableModels);

  import { ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams, execFileSync, spawn } from
  'node:child_process';
  import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
  import { homedir } from 'node:os';
  import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
  
  export interface AdapterSpawnOptions {
    args: string[];
    cwd?: string;
    env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  }
  
  export interface ModelAdapter {
    // Return true if this adapter is available in the current environment
    isAvailable(): boolean;
  
    // Whether this adapter can actually execute a Claude-Code-like session in
    // the current repo. Discovery-only adapters should return false so the UI
    // and API do not silently fall back to another provider.
    supportsExecution?(): boolean;
  
    // Spawn a child process that implements the selected model provider's
    // streaming / CLI behavior. The returned ChildProcess must provide `stdout`
    // and `stderr` streams and support `on('close', ...)`.
    spawn(opts: AdapterSpawnOptions): ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams;
  
    // Optional: discover available model ids for this provider (best-effort).
    // Implementations should return an array of model id strings or an empty
    // array when discovery is not possible.
    discoverModels?: () => Promise<string[]>;
  }
  
  /**
   * Helper to spawn a local process using the same semantics used in the repo.
   * This is provided for convenience in adapter implementations.
   */
  export function spawnLocal(command: string, args: string[], opts:
  AdapterSpawnOptions) {
    return spawn(command, args, {
      cwd: opts.cwd,
      env: opts.env,
      stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
    });
  }

  Perfect — zero raw ARNs anywhere. Here's what was happening and what was
  fixed:
  
  ---
  
  ## What was broken and why
  
  ### 1. `openclaude` — dropdown showed "No models discovered"
  `discoverModels()` tried 4 CLI probes (`openclaude --list-models`, etc.). But
  OpenClaude v0.6 **doesn't support `--list-models`** — it returned an error,
  all 4 probes returned nothing, and the discovery set was empty. With
  "discovered-only" mode on, this showed **"No models discovered"** in the
  dropdown.
  
  **Fix:** Removed the broken CLI probes. Now reads `~/.openclaude/config.json`
  if it exists, tries a single short `openclaude models` probe (exits fast if
  unsupported), then always includes the 3 standard claude names as a guaranteed
  fallback.
  
  ### 2. `occ` — dropdown showed an ugly unreadable Bedrock ARN
  The 5 CLI probes (`occ --list-models`, `occ list-models`, etc.) all
  accidentally launched occ's **interactive REPL**. The REPL printed its startup
  banner, which contained the raw Bedrock ARN:
  `arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:013925090051:inference-profile/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`.
  The heuristic parser picked that up as a "model ID" so the dropdown showed the
  ARN instead of a readable name.
  
  **Fix:** One controlled banner-read probe (no args, reads EOF immediately),
  extracts the short name `claude-sonnet-4-6` from the ARN, always adds the 3
  standard names as fallback.
  
  ### 3. Bedrock ARN leaking from `~/.claude/settings.json`
  Your Claude settings file has the Bedrock ARN as its configured model.
  `collectConfiguredModelIds()` reads that and seeds it into every adapter — so
  even the clean adapters could show the ARN.
  
  **Fix:** Added `normalizeModelId()` + `normalizeModelIds()` helpers to
  ModelAdapter.ts that convert any Bedrock ARN to its readable short name. All
  three adapters now run their seed set through this before returning.
  
  ### 4. `ccr` — was already working
  Reads directly from `~/.claude-code-router/config.json` → returns all 38 LM
  Studio + Ollama models correctly.
  
  **Result:** Reload your dev server and all three providers will show clean,
  readable model names in the dropdown. Compacted conversation

  Here's what I've found so far — a comprehensive diagnosis. Let me now fix the
  CCR config first (the most impactful fix):
  
  ---
  
  ## Root Cause Analysis — 3 Distinct Issues Found
  
  ### Issue 1: CCR Config — Wrong IPs + Transformer Format Bug
  - **LM Studio localhost (127.0.0.1:1234)**: NOT RUNNING — no process, port
  empty
  - **LM Studio LAN**: CCR config has `192.168.1.90` but your Proxmox is at
  `10.2.0.90` — **wrong IP**
  - **Transformer format**: Your config uses `"transformer": ["openai",
  ["maxtoken", ...]]` but CCR v2 expects `"transformer": { "use": ["openai",
  ["maxtoken", ...]] }` — this object-with-`use`-key format is what the official
  docs show
  
  ### Issue 2: http-runner-shim is Single-Shot (NOT Agentic)
  The http-runner-shim.mjs that Ollama/LM Studio adapters use does **ONE** API
  call and exits. Claude Code is a multi-turn agent with tool calling (Read,
  Write, Edit, Bash). Local models via the shim can only return plain text — no
  tool calls, no structured output, no agentic behavior. This is why
  auto-switching breaks — the orchestrator expects rich streaming events.
  
  ### Issue 3: CCR Proxy Server Bug ("Provider 'undefined'")
  Even with CCR running on port 3456, direct API calls return `Provider
  'undefined' not found`. This may be related to the transformer format issue.

  Starting: *Upgrade http-runner-shim to multi-turn agent loop* (6/12)
  
  Now I have the full picture. Here's the key insight:
  
  **The `runClaudeTurn()` function (line 452) handles ALL agent output
  parsing.** It reads `stream-json` events line by line. The critical types it
  handles are:
  - `system` → captures session ID  
  - `assistant` → parses tool_use blocks (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, etc.) and
  text blocks
  - `user` → handles tool_result blocks  
  - `result` → captures final result + usage stats  
  
  **The http-runner-shim already emits `system`, `assistant`, and `result`
  events in the correct format!** So the orchestrator CAN parse the output from
  the shim. The issue is simpler than I thought:
  
  1. **The shim does only ONE call** — it sends the prompt, gets a response, and
  exits. The orchestrator processes that single response correctly, but the
  local model never gets to use tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) because it's not
  in an agentic loop.
  2. **There's NO manual-mode forcing** — the orchestrator uses the same
  `runClaudeTurn()` for ALL providers. It's not treating HTTP providers as
  "manual mode" explicitly; they just complete quickly with a single text
  response.
  
  So the fix is clear: **upgrade http-runner-shim.mjs to support multi-turn tool
  calling** (function calling via OpenAI chat completions format), emitting the
  same stream-json events the orchestrator expects.

  ## ✅ All 12 Tasks Complete
  
  ### Fixes Applied
  1. **CCR Adapter Local-Model Bypass** — The core issue: when the CCR provider
  was selected with a local model (like `llama3.2:latest` or `haiku`), it tried
  spawning `ccr code --model X` which fails because Claude CLI v2.1.119
  validates model names client-side. Fixed with:
     - `isAnthropicModelName()` — detects full IDs and shorthands
  (haiku/sonnet/opus)
     - `findCcrProviderForModel()` — looks up model in CCR config providers
     - `readCcrRouterDefault()` — falls back to Router's default route
     - `spawnViaHttpShim()` — bypasses `ccr code` entirely for non-Anthropic
  models
  
  2. **Agent A Exit Code 1** — Root cause was model name "haiku" failing the old
  regex, not found in CCR providers, and falling through to `ccr code --model
  haiku` which Claude CLI rejected. Fixed by the above.
  
  3. **http-runner-shim v2** (prior session) — Rewritten from single-shot to
  multi-turn agent loop with full tool calling (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob,
  Grep).
  
  4. **CCR LAN IP** — Corrected to 10.2.0.90.
  
  ### Research Findings
  5. **Per-Agent Model Selection** — Feasible (medium complexity). Would need
  `agentModels` map in PipelineState, per-agent lookup in `runClaudeTurn()`, and
  UI per-agent model picker.
  
  6. **Mid-Run Provider Switching** — Easy for between-agent switching (just
  update state file). Complex for mid-agent-turn switching (process management).

  Here's the comprehensive plan:
  
  ---
  
  ## Plan: Local Model Deep Integration Fix
  
  **TL;DR:** Local models (1.2B–3B) fail in pipeline mode due to 3 critical
  bugs: **(1)** the http-runner-shim has **NO session resume support** — every
  agent call starts from scratch, destroying multi-agent continuity (this is the
  #1 reason agents aren't communicating), **(2)** CCR model dropdown doesn't
  show which host/machine models are on, and **(3)** small models can't reliably
  follow the complex role prompts or use tool calling. The fix is phased,
  starting with the resume gap which unblocks everything.
  
  ---
  
  ### Critical Bugs Found
  
  **🔴 BUG #1 — No `--resume` in http-runner-shim (BLOCKS ALL MULTI-AGENT
  COMMUNICATION)**
  - The orchestrator uses `--resume SESSION_ID` for continuity: Agent A plans →
  Agent A resumes to refine → Agent B reviews A's plan → etc.
  - Claude CLI stores conversation history natively. The http-runner-shim
  **completely ignores `--resume`** — every call is a blank conversation.
  - Evidence: `grep resume scripts/http-runner-shim.mjs` = **0 matches**. But
  orchestrator.ts uses `resume:` in **15+ agent calls**.
  - **This is why agents aren't communicating.** Agent A's plan is LOST when the
  orchestrator calls it again, and Agent B gets no context.
  
  **🔴 BUG #2 — CCR Model Dropdown Missing Host Labels**  
  - `discoverModels()` returns flat model names with no host info
  - `liquid/lfm2.5-1.2b` appears in 3 different CCR providers (localhost,
  proxmox, lmstudioLocal) — user can't tell which machine will run it
  - CCR `PROVIDER_FALLBACK_MODELS` only lists Claude models — if discovery
  fails, no local models shown
  
  **🔴 BUG #3 — `findCcrProviderForModel` Picks First Match Blindly**  
  - `liquid/lfm2.5-1.2b` exists in `lmstudioLocalHostMac`, `lmstudio-pmox`, AND
  `lmstudioLocal`
  - Code returns the FIRST match (localhost) — no way to prefer proxmox or check
  which host is responding
  
  **🟡 BUG #4 — Small Models Can't Follow Complex Role Prompts**  
  - Role prompts (role-a.md through role-e.md) are written for Claude-level
  intelligence
  - 1.2B models have tiny context windows, can't follow multi-step instructions,
  and can't reliably produce structured JSON or use tool calling
  - Agent A produces incoherent or empty output → exit code 1
  
  ---
  
  ### Steps
  
  **Phase 1: Diagnostic Tests** (verify current state before changing anything)
  
  1. Test CCR model discovery: `curl localhost:3000/api/models?provider=ccr` —
  verify local models appear  
  2. Test LM Studio reachability: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models` and
  `curl -s http://10.2.0.90:1234/v1/models`  
  3. Test http-runner-shim directly: `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1
  node http-runner-shim.mjs --provider ccr:lmstudioLocal --model
  liquid/lfm2.5-1.2b -p "Say hello"`  
  4. Test Ollama: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`  
  5. Reproduce Agent A failure: start pipeline with ccr + liquid/lfm2.5-1.2b,
  capture logs  
  
  **Phase 2: Fix Session Persistence** (HIGHEST PRIORITY — unblocks multi-agent)
  *depends on Phase 1*
  
  6. Add `--resume SESSION_ID` argument parsing to http-runner-shim.mjs  
  7. Create session storage in `$HOME/.dev-squad-sessions/` — save full
  `messages[]` array as JSON per session  
  8. On `--resume`, load messages from file and prepend to new conversation  
  9. Add context summarization for small models — when session exceeds context
  window, summarize old messages and keep last N  
  10. Verify: run shim twice with `--resume`, confirm conversation continuity  
  
  **Phase 3: Fix CCR Model Discovery + Host Labels** *parallel with Phase 2*
  
  11. Enhance `readCcrConfigModels()` in claudeCodeRouterAdapter.ts to return `{
  model, provider, host }[]`  
  12. Update `/api/models` route to return host info alongside model names

  dependency

  test

  compatible

  - **Scope OUT:** OpenAI HTTP, OpenWebUI, Docker runner, OCC/Bedrock (already
  working)

  ## Plan: Pipeline provider integration & persistence (comprehensive)
  
  TL;DR
  -----
  Ensure UI provider/model selections (including per-agent overrides) are
  authoritative and persisted into the pipeline staging/project state so the
  orchestrator and runner honor them at runtime. Make local HTTP and CLI
  providers reliable for multi-turn agent execution (via adapters and the
  http-runner-shim), add per-provider remediation and CI smoke tests, and harden
  fallback observability so users can see why a provider failed.
  
  Phases (overview)
  -----------------
  - Phase 0 — Discovery & Preparation (quick probes, local environment) —
  output: artifact set + diagnostics (1–4 hours)  
  - Phase 1 — Design & API Contracts (data shapes, guardrails, UX contract) —
  output: precise API & state contract docs (2–6 hours)  
  - Phase 2 — Implementation (server + UI + adapters + runner) — output: code
  changes + docs (1–3 days)  
  - Phase 3 — Testing & Verification (unit/integ/smoke) — output: automated
  smoke checks and manual reproduction steps (6–24 hours)  
  - Phase 4 — CI, Telemetry, and Remediation Docs — output: CI workflow +
  remediation scripts + UI hints (4–16 hours)  
  - Phase 5 — Rollout & Monitoring (canary, verify in staging, manual run) —
  output: production-ready change + monitoring plan (2–8 hours)  
  - Phase 6 — Follow-ups & E2E (playwright tests, QA, long-term improvements) —
  output: E2E suites and backlog items (multi-week)
  
  Phase 0 — Discovery & Preparation
  ---------------------------------
  Objective
  - Collect reproducible environment evidence for provider discovery and runtime
  failures; ensure we understand discovery outputs and current UX storage
  patterns.
  
  Tasks
  1. Run discovery & verification scripts and capture outputs.
  2. Inspect `~/Builds/.staging/pipeline-events.json` and
  `~/Builds/<project>/pipeline-events.json` to confirm presence of
  `selectedModel`, `selectedProvider`, `agentModels`, `events`.
  3. Save diagnostics to `diagnostics/adapter-debug-<ts>.log`.
  
  Commands
  ```bash
  npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
  npx tsx scripts/test-provider-tools-installed.mjs
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs ccr
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs lm-studio
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs ollama
  npx tsx scripts/check-pipeline-state.ts
  ```
  
  Phase 1 — Design & API Contracts
  --------------------------------
  Objective
  - Lock the data contract between UI and server and between
  pipeline-control/orchestrator/runner.
  
  Decisions (recommended)
  - Persist UI choices in pipeline-events.json under: `selectedProvider`,
  `selectedModel`, and `agentModels` (map agent -> model).
  - POST `/api/start-pipeline` accepts `agentModels?: Record<string,string>` and
  `modelProvider?: string`.
  - Orchestrator should use `state.agentModels?.[agent] || state.selectedModel`.
  - Runner should prefer `opts.modelProvider` adapter and write readable
  fallback events to pipeline-events.json on failure.
  
  Files to inspect/update
  - route.ts
  - route.ts
  - pipeline-control.ts
  - orchestrator.ts
  - runner.ts
  - `src/lib/modelAdapters/*`
  
  Phase 2 — Implementation
  ------------------------
  Objective
  - Implement the design with focused, testable commits.
  
  Planned atomic commits
  1. Server: persist model/provider from UI
     - Update `start-pipeline` and chat pipeline handlers to accept `model`,
  `modelProvider`, `agentModels` and persist them via `startPipelineRun()`.
     - Ensure writes to pipeline-events.json are atomic (write temp file then
  rename).
  
  2. Runner/adapters: observability & fallback events
     - HostRunner: attempt `opts.modelProvider` first; on failure write a clear
  fallback event into project pipeline-events.json before falling back.
     - Add a debug log line printing the adapter args before spawn.
  
  3. CCR adapter hardening
     - Ensure `claudeCodeRouterAdapter` uses `spawnViaHttpShim()` for
  non-Anthropic local models and avoid incorrectly treating `--effort` or other
  flags as the trailing prompt.
  
  4. UI per-agent model overrides
     - Add per-agent provider/model selectors to page.tsx and page.tsx.
     - Persist selections to localStorage keys: `devsquad.selectedProvider` and
  `devsquad.selectedModel.<provider>.<agent>`.
     - Wire `usePipelineState().startPipeline(agentModels)` to pass overrides to
  server API.
  
  5. http-runner-shim & HTTP adapters
     - Ensure http-runner-shim.mjs handles OpenAI-compat endpoints and debug
  logging via `HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1`.
  
  6. Docs
     - provider-remediation.md (added) and adapter-deep-dive.md (augment).
  
  Implementation acceptance notes
  - Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before committing.
  - Keep commits small; include a short test recipe in PR description.
  
  Phase 3 — Testing & Verification
  --------------------------------
  Objective
  - Verify discovery, persistence, orchestrator/run, and fallback paths; add
  automated smoke tests.
  
  Commands
  ```bash
  npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
  
  # Provider discovery (per provider)
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs claude-cli
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs ccr
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs occ
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs openclaude
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs ollama
  HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1 npx tsx scripts/test-models.mjs lm-studio
  
  # Pipeline start persistence
  npx tsx scripts/test-start-pipeline-provider-selection.mjs
  npx tsx scripts/check-pipeline-state.ts
  cat ~/Builds/<project>/pipeline-events.json | jq .
  ```
  
  Verification criteria
  - POST `/api/start-pipeline` persists `selectedProvider` and `selectedModel`
  in pipeline-events.json.
  - Orchestrator `runner.spawn()` attempts requested adapter first and writes
  fallback reason to pipeline-events.json if it fails.
  - `agentModels` persisted and used per agent.
  - Regression tests / typecheck pass.
  
  Phase 4 — CI, Telemetry & Remediation
  -------------------------------------
  Objective
  - Catch regressions early and make failures actionable for users.
  
  CI smoke job
  - Add `.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml` to:
    - `npx tsc --noEmit`
    - `npx tsx scripts/check-pipeline-state.ts` (mocked)
    - Run provider discovery in non-blocking mode
  
  Telemetry & observability
  - Write adapter fallback reasons into pipeline-events.json. Add `available:
  boolean` + `reason` to `GET /api/providers`.
  - Surface remediation links in UI when provider unavailable (link to
  provider-remediation.md).
  
  Provider remediation
  - Keep provider-remediation.md updated with per-provider commands and env var
  examples.
  - Add opt-in helper scripts (non-destructive checks only)
  `scripts/fix-provider-<name>.sh`.
  
  Phase 5 — Rollout & Monitoring
  ------------------------------
  Objective
  - Deploy to staging, run smoke runs, observe fallback events; then merge to
  main.
  
  Rollout steps
  1. Branch & PR with focused commits.
  2. Run CI smoke-tests.
  3. Merge to staging/main.
  4. Perform smoke runs for different providers and confirm behavior in
  pipeline-events.json.
  
  Monitoring
  - Check recent pipeline-events.json for fallback messages.
  - Provide maintainers a one-line diagnostic command to find recent fallbacks:
  ```bash
  jq '.events[] | select(.type=="status" or .type=="failure") |
  {time,agent,type,text}' ~/Builds/*/pipeline-events.json | tail -n 40
  ```
  
  Phase 6 — Follow-ups & E2E
  --------------------------
  - Add Playwright tests to exercise per-agent UI and start-pipeline flows.
  - Consider mock adapters for CI to simulate adapter success/failure.
  - Long-term: optional dockerized provider images for CI.
  
  Deliverables
  ------------
  - Code changes to the server, runner, adapters, and UI (listed in plan).
  - provider-remediation.md and adapter deep-dive updates.
  - `.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml`
  - Smoke test scripts leveraged in CI.
  
  Acceptance Criteria
  -------------------
  1. Typecheck passes: `npx tsc --noEmit`.
  2. POST `/api/start-pipeline` persists `selectedModel` & `selectedProvider`.
  3. Orchestrator uses `agentModels` for per-agent overrides and
  `selectedProvider` for adapter preference.
  4. HostRunner attempts requested adapter first; if failing, an explanatory
  fallback is written to pipeline-events.json.
  5. Discovery scripts return model lists for available providers.
  6. CI smoke-tests block PRs on type errors.
  
  Risks & Mitigations
  -------------------
  - CCR will validate model names client-side → mitigation: `spawnViaHttpShim()`
  for non-Anthropic local models and CCR config lookups.
  - Docker image missing or auth errors → readable fallback events + docs for
  Docker.
  - Concurrent writes to pipeline-events.json → atomic write pattern (tmp file
  then rename) and single writer when possible.
  
  Open questions
  --------------
  1. Should pipeline selections be allowed to run if provider is marked
  `available: false`? (Current plan allows but will surface warning.)  
  2. Keep pipeline-events.json as single source of truth or mirror to a team DB?
  (Current plan keeps file authoritative.)  
  3. CI: full provider discovery on every PR is slow — recommended
  discovery-only, non-blocking.
  
  Immediate next steps (if you say “go”)
  --------------------------------------
  1. Implement server persistence changes and small runner logging improvements
  (create small PR). Run typecheck and
  test-start-pipeline-provider-selection.mjs.  
  2. Implement CCR adapter prompt-parsing fix & `http-runner-shim` debug
  improvements (create small PR) and re-run provider tests.  
  3. Add provider remediation docs and CI smoke workflow.
  
  Notes & references
  ------------------
  - Key files: pipeline-control.ts, orchestrator.ts, runner.ts,
  claudeCodeRouterAdapter.ts, route.ts.  
  - Existing helper scripts: test-models.mjs,
  test-start-pipeline-provider-selection.mjs, check-pipeline-state.ts.

  Where variables are set — exact mapping
  - Client-side (UI)
    - Local UI preferences (persisted in localStorage):
      - Key: `devsquad.selectedProvider` — where UI stores the selected provider
  from provider dropdown (now centralized in providerStorage.ts).
      - Key pattern: `devsquad.selectedModel.<provider>` — pipeline-wide model
  per provider.
      - Key pattern: `devsquad.selectedModel.<provider>.<agent>` — per-agent
  model overrides.
    - Files:
      - page.tsx — pipeline view, reads/writes localStorage via
  `providerStorage`.
      - page.tsx — squad view — same usage.
  
  - Client → Server
    - use-pipeline.ts (hook) sends API requests:
      - `startPipeline(securityMode, runGoal, permissionMode, runFinalAudit,
  discoveredOnly, agentModels?)` posts body containing { model, modelProvider,
  agentModels } to `/api/start-pipeline`.
      - `sendChat` posts to `/api/chat` (pipeline-mode chat).
  
  - Server (API)
    - route.ts reads request body (model, modelProvider, agentModels) and calls
  `startPipelineRun(...)` in pipeline-control.ts.
    - route.ts in pipeline mode reads incoming model/modelProvider and persists
  them into the staging state (pipeline-events.json) before launching or
  streaming the agent.
    - route.ts uses adapters to report availability with a `reason` string
  (added) so UI can surface remediation.
  
  - Pipeline control (single source of truth)
    - pipeline-control.ts
      - Writes pipeline state into pipeline-events.json (using atomic writes via
  fileUtils.ts).
      - `createStagingSession(projectDir, opts)` populates the staging file for
  a run.
      - `startPipelineRun(options)` (production path) moves staging state to a
  project folder and spawns the orchestrator (via `spawnOrchestrator`).
  
  - Orchestrator
    - orchestrator.ts:
      - Reads pipeline-events.json and resolves which model/provider to use for
  each agent:
        - model = `state.agentModels?.[agent] || state.selectedModel ||
  DEFAULT_MODEL`
        - provider = `state.selectedProvider`
      - For each agent turn it builds `RunnerOptions` containing model and
  provider, then uses `createRunner()` to spawn an agent process.
  
  - Runner
    - runner.ts:
      - `createRunner()` returns `HostRunner` / `DockerRunner` / `AutoRunner`.
      - `HostRunner.spawn(opts)`:
        - If `opts.modelProvider` set → pick corresponding adapter via
  `getModelAdapter(provider)` and call `adapter.spawn({...})`.
        - If adapter is unavailable or spawn fails, it writes a fallback event
  into pipeline-events.json and falls back to the legacy `claude` CLI or the
  next preferred provider.
      - `DockerRunner.spawn` runs a container; fallback to host worker is
  attempted for recoverable Docker auth issues.
  
  - Adapter layer
    - `src/lib/modelAdapters/*`
      - Each adapter implements `ModelAdapter` interface:
        - `isAvailable()` — local/endpoint health probe (e.g., `which` for CLI
  or ping HTTP endpoint).
        - `supportsExecution()` — whether adapter can run multi-turn sessions.
        - `discoverModels()` — best-effort model list.
        - `spawn(opts)` — actually starts the CLI process or the HTTP shim.
      - Notable adapters:
        - claudeCliAdapter.ts — wraps local `claude` CLI; discovery via `claude
  --list-models`.
        - claudeCodeRouterAdapter.ts — reads
  `~/.claude-code-router/config.json`, can route a local model to an HTTP
  provider and `spawnViaHttpShim()` (uses http-runner-shim.mjs) when model names
  are non-Anthropic.
        - openClaudeAdapter.ts, openClaudeCodeAdapter.ts, openaiHttpAdapter.ts,
  openWebUIAdapter.ts, ollamaAdapter.ts, lmStudioAdapter.ts — each probes and
  spawns as appropriate (HTTP vs CLI).
      - http-runner-shim.mjs — acts as a bridge for HTTP-only providers: adapts
  OpenAI-compatible endpoints to the repo’s stream-json multi-turn runner
  format.
  
  Why CCR / openclaude / Ollama “don’t work” — root causes & fixes
  - Common root causes
    1. CLI binary missing / not on PATH (e.g., `which ccr` returns nothing) →
  adapter.isAvailable() returns false.
    2. Config file missing or incorrect: CCR's
  `~/.claude-code-router/config.json`, openclaude config, or provider-config
  (UI) not set to host/port.
    3. Network endpoint unreachable (wrong port / service not started).
    4. CCR client-side name validation rejects non-Anthropic names (fixed by
  `spawnViaHttpShim()` but requires CCR config or shim).
    5. Argument-parsing heuristics: we fixed a bug where the CCR adapter
  incorrectly popped a trailing `--settings` token and treated flag-like strings
  as prompts (this produced the `--effort '--settings'` error).
    6. Discovery vs runtime mismatch: UI selected provider not yet discovered by
  background discovery; fallback logic prioritized the first provider → UI
  appeared to “reset” to clare-cli. (I changed UI to persist and prefer stored
  provider; further UX improvement: don’t set default until discovery
  completes.)
  
  - Commands to reproduce & debug (quick)
    - Check CLIs:
      ```bash
      which ccr || echo "ccr missing"
      which openclaude || echo "openclaude missing"
      which ollama || echo "ollama missing"
      ```
    - CCR config:
      ```bash
      cat ~/.claude-code-router/config.json | jq .
      ```
    - LM Studio & Ollama HTTP probes:
      ```bash
      curl -sS http://localhost:1234/v1/models | jq .
      curl -sS http://localhost:11434/api/tags | jq .
      ```
    - Run repo diagnostics:
      ```bash
      ./scripts/diagnose-providers.sh
      ./scripts/diag-ccr.sh
      ```
  
  Per-agent model options — how it works and how to add dropdowns
  - Data flow
    - UI per-agent dropdowns set `agentModelOverrides` in the client (persisted
  to localStorage under `devsquad.selectedModel.<provider>.<agent>`).
    - When starting a run, UI calls `startPipeline(..., agentModels)` (I updated
  use-pipeline.ts to accept an `agentModelsArg`).
    - Server `start-pipeline` persists `agentModels` into pipeline-events.json
  (field `agentModels`).
    - Orchestrator uses `state.agentModels[agent] || state.selectedModel` when
  building RunnerOptions.
  - Runtime behavior
    - Each agent turn spawns `runner.spawn()` with the chosen model — so
  multiple agent processes (CLI instances / Docker containers) can be active
  (one per running agent). The runner does not reuse a single CLI window for all
  agents — it spawns per-agent processes per turn.
  - UI additions
    - I added per-agent dropdowns in page.tsx. To also add to page.tsx, we can
  mirror the same controls (I can add those if you want).
  
  Why sometimes agents “don’t see functions” or “tools” do not show up
  - Causes:
    - Adapter does not support execution/tool_use semantics:
  `supportsExecution()` could be `false` (discovery-only).
    - The adapter or http-runner-shim is not providing the stream-json
  `tool_use` events; verify the shim supports them.
    - The model itself or CLI used does not implement the tool/call interface
  expected by the orchestrator.
    - The agent’s role prompt or tool metadata was not passed into the spawned
  child process (args/env).
  - How to confirm:
    - Run orchestrator smoke-run and inspect pipeline-events.json `events` for
  `tool_call` events and provider error messages.
    - Enable `HTTP_SHIM_DEBUG=1` and re-run the runner to see underlying shim
  logs.
  
  Hard-coded models vs discovery — what I changed and recommended next steps
  - Current repo: a small set of provider fallback models existed in route.ts. I
  trimmed large hard-coded lists for LM Studio/Ollama and moved to
  discovery-first UX.
  - Why code used hard-coded lists:
    - Provider discovery can be slow, flaky, or the provider may not be running;
  code used fallback lists to present a usable UX when discovery failed or there
  is no config.
  - Recommended improvement:
    - Always prefer adapter.discovery (adapter.discoverModels()) when available.
    - Cache discovery results for short TTL (e.g., 15–60s) to avoid flakiness
  and reduce UI jitter.
    - Provide explicit manual provider-config UI for host/port (already present)
  with "Test" button that calls discovery and returns every model found.
    - Keep a small fallback list only for providers known to never expose
  discovery.

  Recoverable Error
  
  Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client. As
  a result this tree will be regenerated on the client. This can happen if a
  SSR-ed Client Component used:
  - A server/client branch `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`.
  - Variable input such as `Date.now()` or `Math.random()` which changes each
  time it's called.
  - Date formatting in a user's locale which doesn't match the server.
  - External changing data without sending a snapshot of it along with the HTML.
  - Invalid HTML tag nesting.
  
  It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which
  messes with the HTML before React loaded.
  
  See more info here: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/react-hydration-error

  /**
   * LMStudioAdapter — Adapter for LM Studio local/remote LLM server.
   *
   * Uses LM Studio's APIs in priority order:
   *   1. Native v1 API:   GET <base>/api/v1/models  →  { models: [{ key,
  display_name, ... }] }
   *   2. OpenAI compat:   GET <base>/v1/models       →  { data: [{ id, ... }] }
   *
   * For chat execution, the http-runner-shim uses the OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint
   * at <base>/v1/chat/completions (which LM Studio fully supports).
   *
   * Host/port resolution order:
   *   1. LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL env var
   *   2. Saved provider-config.json (via UI endpoint config panel)
   *   3. Auto-detected from CCR ~/.claude-code-router/config.json lmstudio
  provider
   *   4. Default: http://localhost:1234
   *
   * API docs: https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/rest
   *           https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat
   */
  import path from 'path';
  import { ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams } from 'child_process';
  import {
    AdapterSpawnOptions,
    captureCommandOutput,
    ModelAdapter,
    resolveWorkspacePath,
    spawnLocal,
  } from './ModelAdapter';
  import { getBaseUrlForProvider, getProviderConfig,
  getLmStudioUrlsFromCcrConfig, readProviderConfigs } from '../providerConfig';
  
  /**
   * Returns the LM Studio base URL(s) that match the execution target.
   *
   * Important: discovery should match the endpoint that execution will use.
   * Showing a union of multiple LM Studio hosts in the dropdown is misleading,
   * because the runner only talks to ONE base URL when it actually sends a
  chat.
   *
   * Priority:
   *  1. Env var LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL (only this host)
   *  2. Saved provider-config.json (only this host)
   *  3. First CCR-configured LM Studio host
   *  4. Default: http://localhost:1234
   */
  function getLmStudioBases(): string[] {
    if (process.env.LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL) {
      return [process.env.LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '')];
    }
  
    const saved = readProviderConfigs()['lm-studio'];
    if (saved) {
      return [getBaseUrlForProvider('lm-studio')];
    }
  
    const ccrUrls = getLmStudioUrlsFromCcrConfig();
    if (ccrUrls.length > 0) {
      return [ccrUrls[0].replace(/\/$/, '')];
    }
  
    return ['http://localhost:1234'];
  }
